author: @GabrielReusRodriguez

evidence.api_compatibility: Purely additive — two new keys added to defaults.json and their documentation table. No breaking changes. Existing user configurations are unaffected; new users get sensible defaults (false and 0.9).
evidence.documentation: Updated docs/guide/configuration/README.md with two new table rows including types, defaults, and descriptions. The documentation change matches the code change one-for-one.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The new auto_evict and auto_evict_threshold_pct config keys are user-facing via the lemonade config CLI. No evidence of a human exercising the auto-evict behavior end-to-end (e.g., triggering memory pressure and confirming eviction). However, this PR only ships default values for an existing feature, and the default is auto_evict: false (disabled), so the residual risk for this release is low.
evidence.post_approval_commits: None. The single commit (71ae8485a1e2d12703a58315a017fb2fe7c055e2) was present at both the first and latest approval.
evidence.review: Two maintainer approvals — @jeremyfowers ("Thanks for the fix!", 2026-09-09T14:42:29Z) and @superm1 (empty body, 2026-09-09T19:39:22Z) — on a single-commit PR. The review was brief and neither reviewer has explicit subject-matter expertise in VRAM management per the maintainers table, but the change scope (two config defaults in a JSON file plus docs) is small enough that the minimal review was adequate. No inline comments or requests for changes were raised.
evidence.security: The change adds safe defaults (false for eviction, 0.9 for VRAM threshold). No credentials, network calls, or code execution paths touched. No supply-chain risk.
evidence.tests: No automated tests. The author manually renamed config.json to config.json.old, restarted the server, and confirmed the values appeared via lemonade config. This is reasonable for a change that only adds default values with no new code logic.

verdict_reason: A trivially small, purely additive change (6 lines) with two maintainer approvals, all CI checks passing, no post-approval commits, and documentation updated alongside the code.
